headline: This score ranks the streams of one city by how close they are to a wastewater treatment plant, the one map signal that still held up when it was tested on cities the model had never seen (within-city Spearman 0.22, permutation p = 0.03, across 96 OneAquaHealth lab sites). It says where to look first. It is not a measurement of water quality, it cannot say a stream is safe or unsafe, and it cannot compare one city with another.
description: Map-context baseline v1.1: a single-feature rule. Estimated probability that a stream site is in the top third of OAH lab healthRiskScore, from how close it is to a wastewater treatment plant in OpenStreetMap. A prior for prioritising lab visits, not a measurement.

validated.statement: Ranking sites inside one city is supported by leave-one-city-out: within-city Spearman 0.22 (permutation p = 0.025), within-city AUROC 0.63 (p = 0.03). Comparing absolute scores BETWEEN cities is not supported (pooled AUROC 0.55). Evidence base: 5 European cities, 96 sites, one lab campaign each, so this is one signal tested on five held-out cities, not a validated instrument.

recommendedUse: Order sites within one city (percentile) as a starting prior; citizen event reports and lab results must outweigh it in any referral ranking.

target.name: healthRiskTopTercile
target.definition: healthRiskScore >= 2/3 quantile of the 96 OAH lab sites
target.source: OAH Resilience Map health-risks (one lab campaign per site, 2023-2024)

features.label: Distance to nearest wastewater treatment plant
features.compute: Planar distance from the site point to the nearest WWTP node/way/relation geometry (0 if inside). Searched within city bbox + 25 km; capped at 25 000 m.

contextFeatures.label: Distance to nearest farmland/orchard/vineyard
contextFeatures.compute: Planar distance to the nearest farmland polygon (0 if inside). Searched within bbox + 5 km; capped at 5 000 m.
contextFeatures.expectedDirection: closer = higher risk (not used by v1.1)

contextFeatures.label: Built-up land fraction within 2 km
contextFeatures.compute: Area of the union of built-up landuse polygons inside a 2 km-radius disc, divided by the disc area.
contextFeatures.transform: identity (the JSON also carries urbanFraction2km as a 0-100 percentage for display)
contextFeatures.expectedDirection: more built-up = higher ARG risk (not used by v1.1)

scoring: x = log10(clip(distance to nearest wastewater plant in m, 50, 25000)); z = (x - mean[0])/sd[0]; score = 1/(1+exp(-(intercept + weights[0]*z))). weights[0] is negative, so a closer plant gives a higher score. percentile = percentage of the city's sites with score <= this site's score (0-100).

evaluation.design: leave-one-city-out (Coimbra, Ghent, Toulouse, Benevento, Oslo); transform, threshold and weight refit inside each fold. Within-city metrics use a null that shuffles the target WITHIN each city (1000 times); the across-city metric uses the pooled held-out ranking.

permutationNull.design: target shuffled within each city, 1000 times, whole pipeline refit
target shuffled within each city, 1000 times, whole pipeline refit

baselines.note: The shipped rule IS the single-feature baseline; the multi-feature model it is compared with is under 'alternatives'.

multiFeatureLogistic.whatItWas: The pre-registered v1.0 model: all three features, z-scored in-fold, L2 logistic regression.
multiFeatureLogistic.whyNotShipped: It did not beat chance on a held-out city (pooled AUROC 0.33, permutation p = 0.965). Between-city differences run the wrong way in this sample: Ghent has the closest wastewater plants and farmland but the lowest lab risk, while Benevento has the farthest plants and the highest risk. A model that cannot see the held-out city therefore ranks cities backwards.

oahFeatureVersion.note: The same 3-feature model on OAH's own map features scores better (pooled AUROC 0.70), but that is confounded: OAH's Ghent values look unusable (13 of 17 Ghent lab sites have urbanPct2000m = 0, farmland distances of 0.9-14.9 km although OSM shows farmland 10-460 m away), which happens to push Ghent's scores down to match its low risk.

inFoldFeatureSelection.whatItWas: Pick the feature with the largest |Spearman| inside each training fold.
inFoldFeatureSelection.whyNotShipped: Reported as AUROC 0.72 in v1.0; that figure was an artifact. Each fold emitted the raw transformed feature it selected, so log10-metre values and 0-1 fractions were pooled into a single ranking that mostly encoded which feature the fold had picked. Scored as comparable probabilities the same procedure gives pooled AUROC 0.32, and the selected feature was unstable (urban fraction in Coimbra and Benevento, wastewater distance in Ghent and Oslo, farmland distance in Toulouse).

caveats: What is supported: ordering sites WITHIN one city. What is not: comparing scores between cities, or reading a score as a risk level.
Evidence base is 96 sites in 5 European cities with a single lab campaign each (2023-2024). Five cities means the effective sample for 'does it transfer' is five.
The feature and its direction come from an earlier exploratory pass over these same 96 sites (212 uncorrected tests); leave-one-city-out reduces but does not remove that optimism.
The signal is weak (within-city Spearman about 0.22) and absent in one of the five cities (Ghent).

OpenStreetMap completeness and tagging vary and directly move the score: OSM way 1229453929 'PUB Bukit Timah Waterworks' is tagged man_made=wastewater_plant although it is a drinking-water facility, and it is the nearest 'plant' for 3 of the 10 Singapore sites.

OAH's own map features for Ghent look unreliable (13 of 17 Ghent lab sites have urbanPct2000m = 0, and farmland distances of 0.9-14.9 km although OSM shows farmland 10-460 m away). Worth reporting back to the project.

Out of distribution for tropical cities such as Singapore, where water reclamation plants are sealed facilities discharging to sea rather than into the streams, so the assumed mechanism may not hold. No lab data exists there to check it.
Scores are relative priorities for where to sample, never a safety statement.
